Cassette or Classic Awning? How to Choose for Your Terrace

By the Apex Frames team · October 31, 2026 · 4 min read

Illustrative image

Short answer A cassette awning protects the fabric when retracted and looks cleaner; classic models are simpler. A motor adds comfort, while a manual mechanism is more economical. For larger spaces, an aluminium pergola with or without a canopy is the alternative.

In this article
Cassette or classic
Manual or motorised
What to assess at the technical visit
When a pergola makes sense
Common mistakes
Frequently asked questions

Cassette or classic
Criteria Cassette Classic

Fabric protection The cassette encloses the fabric when retracted The fabric stays more exposed

Look Cleaner Simpler

Best for Strong exposure, frequent use A simpler solution

Manual or motorised
Awnings are offered manual or motorised . A motor makes opening and closing comfortable, especially for large spans; manual is the more economical choice. The fabric is UV-certified material on a strong aluminium structure.

What to assess at the technical visit
the terrace orientation and how much sun it gets;
the wall or structure the awning attaches to and the area it covers;
wind: retract the awning in strong wind;
the fabric colour and how it matches the facade and shutters.

When a pergola makes sense
Aluminium pergolas, with or without a canopy, are made to project and suit large terraces, restaurants and cafés. See also strap and motorised shutters for shading windows.

Common mistakes
Installing without assessing the wall or structure the awning attaches to.
Leaving the awning open in strong wind.
Choosing fabric without UV protection.

Frequently asked questions
Is the fabric sun-resistant?
Yes, we use UV-certified material.
Can I get a pergola without a canopy?
Yes, aluminium pergolas are offered with or without a canopy, to project.
Is a pergola an alternative to an awning?
Yes. For large spaces we offer aluminium pergolas, with or without a canopy, to project.
How protected is the fabric when retracted?
On cassette models, the fabric is enclosed in the cassette when the awning retracts.

an insulated aluminium structure;
double, thermal, solar-control (stop-sol) or laminated glass;
dimensions and divisions per the architect’s design;
custom RAL colours;
weather resistance and sound insulation, with values per the system documentation.

Choosing the glass
Glass Used when

Thermal double Thermal insulation is required

Solar control (stop-sol) The facade gets lots of sun and needs solar control

Laminated Safety is required: see laminated or tempered

For specification we provide technical data sheets and system documentation (DoP, CE), colour samples and visualisations. Learn how to read them in DoP and CE marking .

Technical consulting and system selection for the building.

Installation, final inspection and handover protocol.

## How to Reduce Street Noise with Acoustic Windows | Apex Frames
URL: https://www.apexframes.co/en/blog/reduce-street-noise-with-windows/

Home
Blog
How to Reduce Street Noise with New Windows

Advice

How to Reduce Street Noise with New Windows

By the Apex Frames team · October 31, 2026 · 4 min read

Illustrative image

Short answer Noise insulation depends on four things: the glass (acoustic or laminated), the seals and profile, airtight installation and ventilation. The Rw value in the Declaration of Performance shows the insulation: the higher, the less noise gets through. An open or leaky window cancels the effect.

In this article
What affects sound insulation
How to read the Rw value
What to ask before ordering
Common mistakes
Frequently asked questions

What affects sound insulation
Glass: acoustic glass is built specifically for noise; laminated glass also helps.
Profile and seals: a tight closure blocks sound.
Installation: gaps around the frame let noise in; PU perimeter insulation and quality silicone close them.
Ventilation: an open window insulates nothing.

How to read the Rw value
Rw is the window’s sound-insulation value, expressed in decibels and given in the Declaration of Performance (DoP). The higher the value, the better it insulates. Compare only values from the DoP of the complete system (frame + glass). Learn more in DoP and CE marking .

What to ask before ordering
which acoustic glass is proposed and what the system’s Rw value is;
how installation and perimeter sealing are done: see installation in 8 steps ;
what ventilation options exist when windows stay closed.

Common mistakes
Assuming a new window fixes noise even with weak installation.
Comparing windows without the Rw value from the DoP.
Forgetting ventilation: an open window cancels the insulation.

Frequently asked questions
Is double glazing enough for noise?
It depends. For noisy streets acoustic glass exists; concrete values are given in the Declaration of Performance.
Does installation affect noise?
Yes. Gaps around the frame let noise through, so perimeter insulation and silicone affect the result.
What is Rw?
Rw is the window’s sound-insulation value, in decibels, given in the Declaration of Performance. The higher it is, the less noise gets through.
Is changing the glass enough?
Glass is only one factor: the profile, seals and airtight installation also affect the result.

Related

Glazing
PVC (uPVC) windows & doors
Thermally broken aluminium

Insect Screens: Which Type to Choose for a Door or Window

Choosing products

Insect Screens: Which Type to Choose for a Door or Window

By the Apex Frames team · October 31, 2026 · 4 min read

Illustrative image

Short answer For balcony doors, plissé (pleated) or sliding screens are usually chosen; for windows, vertical roll-up or fixed-frame screens. The mesh is fibreglass or polyester with UV protection, and the modular plissé system has from 1 to 4 leaves.

In this article
The main types
Material and details
What to ask before ordering
Common mistakes
Frequently asked questions

The main types
Type How it works Best for

Horizontal sliding Slides on tracks Windows and doors with space to the side

Vertical roll-up Rolls up into a box Windows

Fixed frame Mounted in a frame and stays in place Windows where the screen isn’t moved often

Plissé (pleated) Folds like an accordion Balcony doors and large openings

Material and details
Mesh: fibreglass or polyester, with UV protection.
Modular plissé system: from 1 to 4 leaves, depending on the opening width.
Low threshold (3–7 mm) on doors, for barrier-free access.
Quality hardware with a magnetic catch.

What to ask before ordering
which model fits your door or window (see also sliding door types );
how much space there is to the side for the screen when open;
how low the door threshold is;
which colour matches the window or door profile.

Common mistakes
Choosing a model without measuring the space to the side.
Overlooking the threshold on doors.
Choosing a colour that doesn’t match the profile.

Frequently asked questions
Which model is best for a balcony door?
Plissé or sliding models are usually used for doors. We choose the model according to the opening and the space to the side during the technical visit.
Is there a low threshold on doors?
Yes, the plissé system for doors has a low threshold (3–7 mm) for barrier-free access.
Are there screens for both windows and doors?
Yes. We offer sliding, vertical roll-up, fixed-frame and plissé models, for doors and windows.
Can I add a screen to an existing window?
It depends on the window and the model; we assess it during the technical visit.

## Privacy Policy | Apex Frames
URL: https://www.apexframes.co/en/privacy/

Home
Privacy Policy
Apex Frames SHPK
Privacy Policy
Last updated 2 November 2026

This policy explains how Apex Frames SHPK (Tax ID M62116046U), registered at Innovation Hub, Pyramid of Tirana, "Dëshmorët e Kombit" Blvd. 5, Tirana, Albania ("we"), processes personal data when you visit www.apexframes.co or contact us. Processing complies with Albanian Law No. 124/2024 on Personal Data Protection and, where applicable, the EU GDPR.

1. Data controller

The controller is Apex Frames SHPK. Questions: info@apexframes.co · +355 69 888 1333.

2. Data we collect

Data you give us by email, phone, WhatsApp or the contact form: name, company, email, phone, project description and site address.

Contract data once you become a client: billing details, measurements, specifications, contracts and correspondence.

Warranty certificate requests (the Warranty certificate page): no personal field is mandatory . You may give your first name, last name, email, phone, product, purchase date and contract or invoice reference; you only need to give at least one detail so we can verify the purchase. We store only what you give. After approval we also keep the certificate number and warranty dates.

This website uses no tracking cookies, analytics or advertising. The contact form does not store data on our server: it simply prepares an email in your own mail app, which you choose whether to send. Unlike it, the warranty certificate form stores the details you fill in in our system (hosted on Netlify) in order to review the request and issue the certificate. To protect against abuse we use a hash of the IP address, not the IP itself, and keep it only for a short time. The request code you receive contains no personal data.

The public certificate check (by AF-… number) shows only the holder’s initials, the dates and the status; the full name, email and phone are never shown.

3. Purposes and legal basis

To answer your request and prepare a quote — pre-contractual steps at your request.

Your consent for the details you voluntarily fill in on the warranty certificate request. You can withdraw consent at any time (info@apexframes.co), without affecting the lawfulness of earlier processing; after approval, keeping the certificate relies on performing our warranty obligation to you.

To perform the contract: survey, manufacturing, installation, handover and warranty, including reviewing the request and issuing the warranty certificate.

To meet legal obligations such as fiscalised invoicing and retention of financial records.

Legitimate interest: protecting our rights and handling complaints.

4. Who we share it with

We never sell your data. We share it only as needed with suppliers and carriers to fulfil your order, with email and hosting providers, with our accountant, or with authorities where required by law. All act under written agreements and confidentiality obligations.

Transfers outside Albania. The certificate system is hosted by Netlify, Inc. (USA), and automatic emails (if enabled) are sent through an email provider. Data may be stored or processed outside Albania. These transfers rely on the provider’s data processing agreement and the standard contractual clauses it includes. The website does not transfer data to social networks without your action.

5. Retention

Enquiries that do not lead to a contract are kept for up to 12 months. Certificate requests that are not approved (pending or rejected) are deleted automatically after 12 months. Issued certificates are kept during the warranty (5 years); 12 months after expiry the personal data is deleted or anonymised and only the number, dates and status remain, with no personal data. You can ask for earlier erasure. Contract and financial documents are kept for at least 5 years under Albanian tax law.

6. Your rights

You may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction, data portability, object to processing, and withdraw consent you have given. Write to info@apexframes.co ; we reply within 30 days. You may also lodge a complaint with the Albanian Commissioner for the Right to Information and Personal Data Protection (idp.al).

7. Security

We apply reasonable technical and organisational measures: access limited to authorised staff, communication from official company addresses and structured document archiving. The internal certificate panel is password-protected and access is limited to authorised staff. In case of a personal data breach that poses a risk, we notify the Commissioner within 72 hours and, where the risk is high, the affected individuals.

8. Changes

We may update this policy. The version in force is always the one published on this page, with its update date.
